item.text: {"search_note":"Overall: evidence is strongly negative. I found repeated reporting of arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killing, torture/ill-treatment, and abusive parallel security structures, but little credible evidence that Abiy meaningfully prevented or punished those abuses. The best positive material is limited to oversight/institution-building rhetoric, EHRC complaint mechanisms, ICRC training, and transitional-justice messaging. Bottom line: I found weak positive evidence of formal accountability structures and rhetoric, but strong negative evidence that police, military, intelligence, and parallel security actors were committing abuses with limited restraint, little visible punishment, and in some cases apparent state tolerance. I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Abiy publicly disciplined major abusive commanders or credibly held security forces to account for Merawi, arbitrary detentions, or attacks on civilians and medical care.","evidence":[{"title":"Country policy and information note: actors of protection, Ethiopia, February 2024","publisher":"GOV.UK","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible","summary":"The note says the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission receives complaints and that some state/federal institutions implemented its recommendations on human-rights protections and prison conditions. This is weak positive evidence of some accountability infrastructure, but it does not show Abiy actually punished abusive forces.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopian Justice Minister Briefs Diplomats about Transitional Justice Policy Implementation","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-12-14","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876","summary":"The government said the transitional justice policy is meant to address accountability, truth-seeking, conditional amnesty, reconciliation, and institutional reform. This supports a stated commitment to remedy abuses, but it is process rhetoric, not proof of punishment or restraint in practice.","question_ids":["3B.2","2B.7","3B.1"]},{"title":"ICRC Bulletin: Ethiopia, January-June 2024","publisher":"International Committee of the Red Cross","date":"2024-09-13","url":"https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024","summary":"The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for the ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups, aiming to improve protection of civilians and medical personnel. That is a limited positive sign, but it shows training and engagement rather than actual punishment of abuse.","question_ids":["3B.2","2B.7","3B.1"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-04-04","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region","summary":"HRW reported Ethiopian forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi and other abuses by federal forces operating with impunity. I found no public sign that Abiy accepted responsibility or imposed accountability for these killings.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-07-03","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict","summary":"HRW documented soldiers beating, arresting, and intimidating medical staff, seizing ambulances, and attacking medical transport. The report also says abusive forces were operating with near impunity, which cuts against any claim that the government was effectively preventing or punishing them.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-10-01","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/","summary":"Amnesty said the army and police were carrying out arbitrary mass detentions without warrants and often without timely court appearance. This is direct evidence of abuse by state security forces, with no visible accountability response from Abiy.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC / Reuters investigation cited by EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"The EHRC head confirmed the existence of the secret “Koree Nageenyaa” committee and said it overreached by interfering in the justice system with widespread human-rights violations. This is strong evidence of a tolerated or politically shielded coercive apparatus, not effective prevention or punishment.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1","2B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: The Deepening Crackdown on Dissent","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-04","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent","summary":"HRW reported arbitrary arrests, forced disappearance of EHRCO staff, and broad repression of critics. That indicates security-force abuse tolerated by the state rather than prevented or sanctioned.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-06-18","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups","summary":"Security and intelligence personnel reportedly followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers, including at homes and offices. This is direct evidence of abusive conduct by state agents that was not visibly curbed by Abiy.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.1"]}]}
